{{Short description|Constant in algebraic geometry}}

In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''Seshadri constant''' is an invariant of an [[ample line bundle]] <math>L</math> at a point on an [[algebraic variety]]. It was introduced by [[Jean-Pierre Demailly]] to measure a certain "rate of growth" of the [[tensor power]]s of <math>L</math> in terms of the [[jet (mathematics)|jets]] of the [[Section (category theory)|sections]] of the <math>L^k</math>. The object was the study of the [[Fujita conjecture]]. The constant's name stems from its connection to [[C. S. Seshadri]]'s criterion for ampleness.{{sfnp|Lazarsfeld|2004|p=270}}

It is known that [[Nagata's conjecture on algebraic curves]] is equivalent to the assertion that for more than nine general points, the Seshadri constants of the [[projective plane]] are maximal. There is a general conjecture for [[algebraic surfaces]], the [[Nagata–Biran conjecture]].

==Definition==
Let <math>X</math> be a smooth [[projective variety]], <math>L</math> an [[ample line bundle]] on <math>X</math>, <math>x</math> a point of <math>X</math>, and <math>\mathcal{C}_x</math> the set of all irreducible curves passing through <math>x</math>. Define the ''Seshadri constant'' of <math>L</math> at <math>x</math> by{{sfnp|Lazarsfeld|2004|p=270}}
:<math>\varepsilon(L,x) = \inf_{C \in \mathcal{C}_x} \frac{L \cdot C}{\operatorname{mult}_x(C)}</math>,

where <math>L \cdot C</math> denotes the [[intersection number]] of <math>L</math> and <math>C</math> and <math>\operatorname{mult}_x(C)</math> measures how many times the curve <math>C</math> passes through <math>x</math>.

If <math>X</math> is an [[abelian variety]], then <math>\varepsilon(L,x)</math> is independent of the point <math>x</math> chosen, and we write simply <math>\varepsilon(L)</math>.
